text:
Not that Elias Pettersson. The Canucks' 22-year-old defenseman shares a name with the centre in every trade rumor, which means his own headlines get buried. This one is a third-round pick from 2022, playing about 19 minutes a night in his second full season, with three goals and four points in 22 games, 46 hits and 34 blocks.

His three goals came early and are worth more than they look: by our count they added about two-thirds of a win to Vancouver's season, more than the chances behind them. Since late October he has one assist. The play around him has been hard. Vancouver takes only 41% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, though that's slightly better than the team does without him, and his pairing with Filip Hronek has taken about 37% of the chances.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with opponents creating a lot against him, but also noted he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found only 31% of his exits keep possession. Our talent range has him around 16 points. On a rebuilding team, his minutes are the development plan.
